title: GLM-4.6
hook: Zhipu's GLM-4.6 is an open-weight MoE that became a popular drop-in coding backend — near Claude Sonnet 4 on real-world coding, with a 200K context and a permissive license.
key_points: Zhipu AI's open-weight model, released September 2025 under an MIT license.
Tuned for real-world coding, long-context work, reasoning, and agentic tool use.
Reported near parity with Claude Sonnet 4 on multi-turn coding evaluations.
content_html: GLM-4.6, from Beijing-based Zhipu AI, is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model released in late September 2025 under a permissive MIT license. With 355 billion parameters and a 200K-token context window, it was tuned heavily for real-world coding and agentic work, and it found traction as an affordable, self-hostable backend for coding agents.
extra_html:
What's new

GLM-4.6 emphasized practical coding strength over leaderboard chasing: Zhipu reported it near parity with Claude Sonnet 4 on multi-turn coding tasks evaluated by humans in isolated environments, while using fewer tokens than its predecessor to finish jobs. It pairs a long context with reasoning, search, and tool-use improvements, and ships open weights that run on common serving stacks like vLLM and SGLang.

Why it matters

GLM-4.6 is part of a wave of strong open-weight Chinese models — alongside DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi — that closed much of the gap with closed frontier labs on coding specifically. For developers, an MIT-licensed model that approaches a top closed model on coding, at far lower cost and fully self-hostable, is a compelling backend for agentic tools.
